hook: An open door offers little freedom if leaving would cost you everything.
readerPromise: Explore usable freedom and proportionate responsibility through the practical conditions of ordinary choice.
protectedRevelations: Final normative framework and policy recommendations
visualPlan: Can you use the open door?: Show an open doorway beside a person whose necessary belongings and care duties keep them from leaving. Keep the permission and the usable path as separate parts of the same situation. Place several people before the same open door with different resources and obligations.

The conditions behind a choice: Connect the doorway to work, citizenship and care through ordinary documents and a dependent person. Show a resignation letter beside the unanswered question of housing and income afterward. Let two people consider their different capacities to help without deciding their obligations by appearance.
Freedom among other people: Bring the shared supports for a usable choice into the space beside the door. End with the open doorway and the real conditions needed to cross it.

cueChanges.nextVisualChange: Replace abstract choice symbols with the same open doorway approached by people with different practical constraints.
Show a work commitment and its available exit without implying that every dependency is coercive.
Return to the doorway with people still connected to one another; end on capacity rather than a victory gesture.

sentenceIntentions.text: An open door offers little freedom if leaving would cost you everything.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Make formal exit unusable through prohibitive cost
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Feel the practical limit of an open door

sentenceIntentions.text: Freedom and Its Price asks what makes a choice usable, and what responsibility can reasonably demand.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Name usable choice and fair responsibility together

sentenceIntentions.text: Its starting scene gives several people the same permission while their capacities and dependencies remain different.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Give equal permission alongside unequal capacities
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Recognize why identical rules may not mean equal freedom

sentenceIntentions.text: From there, the book moves through work, citizenship, care, and power inside choices that seem voluntary.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Locate dependence in work, citizenship and care
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: See apparently private choice as institutionally shaped

sentenceIntentions.text: A right to resign and a realistic way to survive resignation are not the same protection.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Contrast resignation rights with survival after resignation
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Grasp a concrete distinction between permission and capability

sentenceIntentions.text: Knowing another person's limits still leaves hard questions about what each of us owes the other.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Keep limits from settling reciprocal obligations automatically
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Feel the question remain morally demanding

sentenceIntentions.text: Choices that feel private turn out to depend on conditions people must build and protect together.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Give language to personal choices supported by shared conditions
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Recognize the relevance to everyday decisions

sentenceIntentions.text: Begin at the doorway, and consider who can actually walk through it.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Return to who can cross the doorway
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Want to inspect freedom from the affected person's position

distinctiveContribution: Freedom and responsibility are joined through unequal capacities, dependencies and the material conditions making permission usable.
